title: What are the lines called when all four angles are equal?
description: Two lines cross so that all four angles are equal. A linear pair adds up to one hundred and eighty degrees, so each angle is ninety degrees, and the lines are named. Keeko doubts that each angle is forty five degrees.
teaching_notes: One idea: a linear pair of equal angles shares one hundred and eighty, so each angle is ninety degrees and the lines are perpendicular. Watch for students who share one hundred and eighty among all four angles.

source: Two lines cross so that all four angles are equal. Find each angle, and say what the lines are called.
video_script.why: The child finds the size of each angle from the straight line and meets the name for lines that cross like this.
video_script.substitution: The book's own question about intersecting lines with four equal angles: two neighbours form a linear pair, so each angle is half of one hundred and eighty.
video_script.anchor: Two lines crossing so that all four angles look equal, with the four angles named a, b, c and d going round.
video_script.wrong_answer: each angle is forty five degrees
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko shares one hundred and eighty among all four angles.
video_script.payoff_line: Each angle is ninety degrees, and the lines are perpendicular.

final_answer.value: Each angle is 90°, and the lines are perpendicular
final_answer.spoken: each angle is ninety degrees, and the lines are perpendicular

hold_back: Each angle is 90°, and the lines are perpendicular
maths_rules: two neighbouring angles are a linear pair: a + b = 180
the angles are equal, so a = b and each is 180 / 2 = 90
all four angles are equal, so all four are 90, right angles
lines that intersect at right angles are perpendicular, however the pair is tilted
the slip: 180 / 4 = 45 shares the straight line among four angles, but only two angles lie on one straight line
video_script.design: One crossing stays on the stage with its four equal angles. A linear pair lights up, the straight line of 180 is split into two equal halves, and the square corner symbol is placed on the crossing.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks each angle is forty five degrees, because four angles share one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But one hundred and eighty belongs to only two neighbours on a straight line.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The other two angles lie on their own straight line. Each angle is ninety degrees.
